name: Single Fling
description: The hatchet slips from the belt loop into a hammer grip in one pull, already angled to cut.

name: Leaden Spikepoll
description: A chop driven from the elbow drops the bit onto the opponent's forearm or shoulder at arm's length.

name: Kept Tailknob
description: The haft meets an incoming blade at a slant so the edge slides off toward the ground.

name: Hurl Lid
description: The hooked beard snags a raised wrist or shield rim and tugs it aside to open the guard.

name: Chuck Trot
description: A short two-foot shuffle closes the last pace to the target without crossing the feet.

name: Square Lob
description: From a planted stance the hatchet is thrown overarm, turning once before the bit lands on a target a few paces away.

name: Birchcowl
description: The student squares to a braced guard with the hatchet held high and the free forearm covering the ribs.

name: Hard Balancepoint
description: Repeated single chops into a stump teach the wrist to land the bit edge-first and never flat.

name: Flintdash
description: The blunt poll swings short and knocks the helm or skull, stunning an opponent without opening the skin.

name: Sudden Edgecurve
description: At four paces the axe turns half a revolution in flight and lands bit-first in the torso.

name: Leaden Thumbnotch
description: A flick of the wrist at the end of the arc sets the spin so the axe flies true instead of tumbling.

name: Flintpause
description: One pace back with the haft raised across the face turns a thrown blade or club aside.

name: Sideways Tomahead
description: After a throw the student sprints to the stump and wrenches the axe free for the next toss.

name: Lobhit
description: The axe is drawn from the opposite hip across the body and chops outward in the same motion.

name: Tosscowl
description: Gripping close under the head, the user hooks the beard behind an elbow and drags the arm out of line.

name: Single Quickbit
description: A level swing at thigh height bites the bit into the outer leg of an opponent rushing past.

name: Birchwedge
description: A sidestep takes the body off the line while both fists on the haft stop a downward blow.

name: Lobstrike
description: A low underhand toss sends the axe spinning flat at the shins of an opponent two paces off.

name: Tossbump
description: Sliding the hand down the haft mid-swing lengthens the arc so the bit lands a hand's breadth farther than expected.

name: Narrow Lightbit
description: A rolled wrist turns the axe over so a backhand chop follows a forehand cut without a pause.

name: Toss Strike
description: The butt of the haft jabs into the belly as a short distraction before the real cut.

name: Towing Pitch
description: The beard hooks behind an ankle and the haft pulls it forward, throwing the opponent off balance.

name: Hard Tomahead
description: At eight paces the axe makes one full turn before the bit strikes the target's chest.

name: Straight Spikepoll
description: A sidearm throw sends the axe spinning flat across the ground at waist height toward a line of foes.

name: Settled Throwhelve
description: Wrists crossed over the haft, the user catches a downward cut and steers it clear of the head.

name: Swaying Chuck
description: A pivot on the ball of the lead foot turns the body out of a charge while the axe stays ready.

name: Short Birchhelve
description: In a clinch, short rapid chops land the bit on the shoulder and neck guard where long blades cannot swing.

name: Flinghusk
description: The beard traps a spear shaft or sword hilt and a twist of the wrist strips it from the hand.

name: Narrow Quickbit
description: The poll hammers the side of the knee, buckling the stance so a follow-up cut can land.

name: Settled Lightbit
description: The haft held overhead stops a downward blow while the free hand clamps the opponent's wrist.

name: Sideways Throwhelve
description: A slipping step off the centre line lets the opponent's blow miss as the user chops in the same motion.

name: Wide Pitch
description: A full-body lean drives the axe ten paces in two turns, enough to bite through a leather jerkin.

name: Flintwedge
description: A thread of qi sent into palm and fingers keeps the grip firm when a heavy blow strikes the haft.

name: Birchdrop
description: A small pulse of qi along the haft adds weight to a chop so the bit bites deeper.

name: Descending Birchhelve
description: Qi gathered in the wrist at release holds the axe's spin tight so the throw flies true.

name: Lobbump
description: At twelve paces the axe spins twice and lands bit-first, its steadiness owed to qi at release.

name: Shifting Tailknob
description: Qi in the calves lengthens a backward step, buying room to throw before the opponent closes.

name: Holding Thumbnotch
description: The lightly charged haft slaps a thrown knife or dart out of its path.

name: Turning Toss
description: A qi-lightened pull on the hooked beard snaps the opponent's weapon arm out of line.

name: Balancepoint Dash
description: The thrower counts turns by distance so the bit arrives edge-first at any range.

name: Forward Fling
description: The axe is released high and drops steeply onto a target behind a low barrier or raised shield.

name: Leaden Chuck
description: A low level throw skims above the ground and cracks into the shins of a runner.

name: Stepping Thumbnotch
description: A dodge to the side clears an incoming strike while the other hand draws a second axe.

name: Ready Edgecurve
description: The axe's flat turns a descending sword onto the haft and slips it past the shoulder.

name: Flintstay
description: The beard grips the top of a shield and pulls it down, exposing the face behind it.

name: Open Birchhelve
description: A poll blow rings off the helm and dazes the wearer even where the edge cannot cut.

name: Throwhelve Bump
description: The spike on the poll is driven into the gap of an armor joint with a pulse of qi.

name: Fixing Balancepoint
description: With the beard hooked over a spear shaft the user steps back and drags the point off line.

name: Birchhusk
description: Both hands on the haft and the head held high, the user braces against a heavy overhead strike.

name: Quick Edgecurve
description: After hooking a limb, the axe turns in the hand and chops down onto the trapped forearm.

name: Tossdodge
description: After a throw the user steps to the target and wrenches the axe out with a levered twist of the haft.

name: Pitchblow
description: Two axes are thrown in quick succession, the second leaving the other hand while the first is still turning.

name: Hurl Hit
description: A running throw carries the user's momentum into the axe, adding force without a planted stance.

name: Narrow Toss
description: From a crouched low guard a backhand throw sends the axe at the opponent's lead knee.

name: Lowered Tailknob
description: Qi in the forearms steadies the haft so a heavy club or maul stops dead against it.

name: Light Fling
description: A forward roll beneath a swing ends within chopping range, the axe drawn as the user rises.

name: Chucklid
description: The beard catches a cloak or sash and yanks, pulling the opponent's stance off balance.

name: Headlid
description: A feigned throw makes the opponent flinch or duck, and the axe is chopped downward in the same motion.

name: Blunt Tomahead
description: The axe is thrown while skipping sideways, so the target cannot read the line of release.

name: Firm Hurl
description: A loose-wristed whip of the haft lands a fast cut on an exposed hand or wrist.

name: Birchstrike
description: While backing away, the user turns at the waist and hurls the axe at the pursuer's chest.

name: Lightbit Skitter
description: A quick dart between two opponents puts the user at the flank of one and out of the other's reach.

name: Hooding Throwhelve
description: Held edge-down with the haft slanting out, the axe turns a cut aside and into the ground.

name: Tossstay
description: A sharp rap of the haft on the weapon wrist loosens the opponent's grip for an instant.

name: Tripping Edgecurve
description: A hurried throw sent past the opponent's ear makes them duck and give ground.
